stem:
Kariba Kapenta Packers dries and packs kapenta for supermarkets. For 2026 the budget was to produce 10,000 packs and the budgeted fixed production overhead was US\$45,000. The business absorbs fixed production overhead on the budgeted number of packs. Other information:

| Item | US\$ |
| --- | ---: |
| Selling price per pack | 14 |
| Direct materials per pack | 2.70 |
| Direct labour per pack | 1.90 |
| Variable production overhead per pack | 0.40 |
| Variable selling cost per pack sold | 0.70 |
| Actual fixed production overhead for the year | 46,200 |
| Administration expenses for the year | 19,000 |

Opening inventory was 1,000 packs, valued at the same full production cost per pack as in 2026. Actual production was 9,400 packs and sales were 9,900 packs.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the fixed production overhead absorbed per pack.
parts.explanation: 45,000 ÷ 10,000 = US\$4.50 a pack. Using the actual output or the actual overhead gives a rate that is not pre-determined.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 45,000 ÷ 10,000 = US\$4.50 a pack. Using the actual output or the actual overhead gives a rate that is not pre-determined.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the full production cost per pack.
parts.explanation: 2.7 + 1.9 + 0.4 + 4.5 = US\$9.50. Selling cost is not a production cost.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 2.7 + 1.9 + 0.4 + 4.5 = US\$9.50. Selling cost is not a production cost.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the number of packs in closing inventory.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the fixed production overhead absorbed during the year.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Compare the overhead absorbed with the actual fixed production overhead.

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: Calculate the amount of the difference.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: The difference is:

options.content: over-absorbed, so it is added to profit
options.rationale: Absorbed overhead is less than actual.

options.content: under-absorbed, so it is deducted from profit
options.rationale: Correct: absorbed overhead is less than actual.

options.content: under-absorbed, so it is added to profit
options.rationale: Under-absorption is a charge against profit.

options.content: over-absorbed, so it is deducted from profit
options.rationale: Absorbed overhead is less than actual.

parts.explanation: The overhead absorbed is less than the overhead incurred, so it is under-absorbed and reduces profit.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Calculate the value of the closing inventory.

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: Prepare the absorption costing profit statement for the year ended 31 December 2026.

points.description: Cost of sales 94,050: opening inventory plus production less closing inventory at the full cost
Selling costs 6,930 and administration expenses 19,000 deducted

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Kariba Kapenta Packers: absorption costing profit statement**

|  | US\$ | US\$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Sales (9,900 × US\$14.00) |  | 138,600 |
| Opening inventory (1,000 × US\$9.50) | 9,500 |  |
| Production cost (9,400 × US\$9.50) | 89,300 |  |
| Closing inventory (500 × US\$9.50) | (4,750) |  |
| Cost of sales |  | (94,050) |
| Under-absorbed fixed production overhead |  | (3,900) |
| **Gross profit** |  | 40,650 |
| Selling costs (9,900 × US\$0.70) |  | (6,930) |
| Administration expenses |  | (19,000) |
| **Profit** |  | 14,720 |

parts.explanation: One mark for each line or group of lines; allow follow-through.

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: State the profit for the year under absorption costing.

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: A manager prefers marginal costing. Calculate the profit under marginal costing and explain the difference from your answer to (h).

points.description: The difference is 2,250, equal to the fall in inventory (500 packs) × US\$4.50
Marginal profit is higher because inventory fell, so absorption costing charged fixed overhead from the opening inventory

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Contribution 82,170 less fixed costs 65,200 gives a profit of 16,970. This is 2,250 higher than the absorption profit because inventory fell by 500 packs, each carrying US\$4.50 of fixed overhead, which absorption costing released into cost of sales.

explanation: This ZIMSEC Paper 2 style question tests the absorption rate, inventory, under-absorption and the absorption costing profit statement, with a comparison with marginal costing.

stem:
Chinhoyi Dairy makes tubs of yoghurt. The selling price is US\$3.50 a tub. Variable costs are US\$2.10 a tub (including variable selling costs) and fixed costs are US\$56,000 a year. Budgeted sales for 2026 are 50,000 tubs. The following table was prepared for the owner:

| Output (tubs) | Revenue US\$ | Total cost US\$ | Profit or (loss) US\$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 0 | 56,000 | (56,000) |
| 20,000 | 70,000 | 98,000 | (28,000) |
| 40,000 | 140,000 | 140,000 | 0 |
| 60,000 | 210,000 | 182,000 | 28,000 |

Give percentages to one decimal place.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the contribution per tub.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the contribution to sales ratio, as a percentage.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the break-even point in tubs.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the break-even point in sales revenue.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Calculate the margin of safety in tubs.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Calculate the margin of safety as a percentage of budgeted sales.

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: Calculate the number of tubs that must be sold to earn a profit of US\$28,000.

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: Using the table, at which output do revenue and total cost become equal?

options.rationale: There is a loss of US\$28,000 at this output.
A profit of US\$28,000 is made at this output.
At nil output the loss equals the fixed costs.

parts.explanation: Revenue equals total cost (profit nil) at 40,000 tubs.

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: The owner proposes to cut the price to US\$3.20 so that sales rise to 62,000 tubs. Costs are unchanged. Calculate the profit under this proposal.

parts.label: (j)
parts.stem: Advise the owner whether to cut the price. The budgeted profit at US\$3.50 is US\$14,000. Refer to your figures and give one non-financial factor and one limitation of the analysis.

points.description: The proposal gives 12,200, which is less than the budgeted 14,000
The lower price cuts the contribution per tub from 1.40 to 1.10, and the extra sales do not make up for it
Recommend not cutting the price (keep the present price)
Non-financial: a lower price may harm the image of the brand, or the extra volume may not be achievable
Limitation: break-even analysis assumes constant costs and sales forecasts that may not be achieved

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The price cut gives a profit of 12,200 against the budget of 14,000, because the contribution falls to US\$1.10 a tub. The owner should keep the present price. A lower price may also damage the brand, and the sales forecast of 62,000 tubs may not be reached.

explanation: This ZIMSEC Paper 2 style question tests break-even, margin of safety, target profit and an evaluation of a price change.
hints: Margin of safety uses budgeted sales as the base.
